title: Recursive characterization of canonical integral realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. On the small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes use the strict semilinear system categories $\mathscr S_W$, reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W$, and actual adjunction unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use the operations $P_v,S_p,J_j,\otimes^L$ and their integral counterparts from [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], with $v$ separated finite type, $p$ proper and $j$ quasi-compact open. Restrict all input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Let $d_A$ be exactly the single-operation identification of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], including its specified localized open comparison. On these domains $u_K$ and $e_M$ are invertible. The canonical realization comparisons $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] are characterized by the following identities. For a variable, $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$. For a unary basic operation set
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal L M)\circ(\mathcal L A(e_M))^{-1}:\mathcal L A(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(\mathcal L M).$$
For tensor set
$$a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal L M,\mathcal L N)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^L e_N)\bigr)^{-1}:\mathcal L(M\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L M\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal L N.$$
For $M=V(\mathcal R K_i)$ and $N=T(\mathcal R K_i)$, with independent leaf slots, the identities are
$$c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)\circ a_A(M),\qquad c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)\circ a_\otimes(M,N).$$
All these identities are natural in the input morphisms. This characterizes the specified comparisons themselves, including their normalization at a variable; it asserts no compatibility with shifts.

proof.text: Apply actual normalized reconstruction to Good systems, obtaining invertibility of the actual counit. For an sf-derived-complete integral input use the intrinsic/legacy completeness comparison with an auxiliary finite-field datum in universe zero; actual reconstruction then makes its unit invertible. This does not change any domain or boundedness hypothesis.

The right triangle identity gives u_(LM) followed by L(e_M) equal to identity. Since e_M is invertible, u_(LM) is invertible and its specified inverse is L(e_M). Substitute this in properD. Naturality of the recorded realizationModel.push at e_M cancels the inverse-counit factor in properA, leaving exactly the recorded proper comparison at M.

For the open operation, transport invertibility of u_(LJM) along the given openRealization isomorphism by unit naturality. The openNormalization field says L J(e_M) followed by openRealization and the actual unit equals L(openReduction). Cancel the two now invertible outside factors. The resulting identity is exactly openA = openRealization, with the specified localized openD.

The preceding identities make properA and openA invertible. PullA and tensorA are composites of the inverse of a functor applied to one counit or the pair of counits, followed by precisely the natural pullD and tensorD isomorphisms defined in the generator-reduction interface. Together with the actual unit/counit results these prove OperationLaws.

Induct on Expression restricted by BasicTree. At a variable cancel inputNormalization to identify the component with inverseOrZero of the actual unit. At a pull or tensor vertex cancel the invertible image of the counit (respectively pair of counits) in the pull or tensor field of Realizations. At a proper or open vertex use step 2 or 3 and the push or shriek field. Restrict to the child full domains exactly as in Equations and combine with the induction hypotheses. CompactSupport is excluded by BasicTree.

For any second family satisfying Equations, induct on the same tree to prove equality of hom components: leaves have the same inverse unit, each unary map follows by functorial congruence from its child, and tensor follows from both child equalities in their independent slots. Extensionality of natural transformations and of isomorphisms gives equality of the specified natural isomorphisms. Their naturality is already part of their types.
